To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing

The cover note says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened", and reflect "standard and widely accepted market terms." **We should not accept any of this.**

- **Nothing has been agreed through our authority process.** No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for any fallback (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3). A counterparty's statement that terms were agreed does not make them agreed.
- **"Market standard" is an assertion, not a reason.** Each position must be tested against our playbook on its merits.
- **The cover note contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** For example, it says Bluefen is "addressed", but DL §2 says no consent or condition evidence exists. It calls the incident "not expected to be material", but DL §6 says scope, access and notification are all undetermined. Where they conflict, we should rely on the Disclosure Letter's factual statements and treat the cover note as advocacy.
- **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. We need a bring-down update on every open item before relying on any of it.

**Recommended response:** state in writing that Wattlebridge does not regard any position as agreed or final, and that all points remain open pending our mark-up.

---

## Material departures from the playbook

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Issue:** the figure matches our fallback number, which may make it look cleared. It is not. A matching number does not clear the change, and the Seller has also bundled it with much worse terms (thresholds, time limits, fundamental collapse, no fraud carve-out). A 20% cap inside this package is worth far less than 20% inside our structure.
- **Push back:** restore 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not concede 20% unless Amelia Frost authorises it in writing for this draft, and only if the rest of the regime matches the playbook.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, deductible basket AUD 250k
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; once exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar (tipping basket).
- **Issue:** the de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The basket is also a deductible ("only the excess"), so the first AUD 250k of every proven loss is permanently absorbed by us. A high de minimis also excludes many claims from counting towards the basket at all.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis. Related claims arising from the same facts should aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, applied to "all Claims"
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Fundamental claims run at least 6 years.
- **Issue:** the drafting that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a **hidden general-regime override**. By default it sweeps Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general limits.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Reverse the default so that limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Keep separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties collapsed into the general regime
- **Playbook:** separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** "administrative simplicity" is not a justification. Under the Seller's draft, if the Seller does not own the shares, our recovery is capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price, subject to a AUD 250k deductible and 18 months.
- **Push back:** reject outright and reinstate the separate fundamental regime.

### 5. Fraud is not carved out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- **Issue:** "apply to all Claims of any nature" on its face extends limitations and non-reliance to fraud and wilful concealment. Some protection may exist at law regardless, but we should not rely on that or leave the point to argument.
- **Push back:** this is non-negotiable and is not a trading point. Insert an express carve-out across caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance and the buyer-knowledge and disclosure provisions.

### 6. General disclosure (DL §1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** DL §1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, and §1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Together these would neutralise most warranties.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete §1.1 and §1.2.
  - Disclosures must be specific, fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and referenced against the relevant warranty.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Title/capacity warranties or specific indemnities.
  - Treat DL §1.4 (non-admission) as acceptable only if it cannot be used to argue that a known issue was "disclosed" for indemnity purposes.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** cl 8.3 is maximally broad. It covers knowledge of the Buyer *or its advisers*, and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Combined with the general disclosure, it would bar claims for the very risks we identified in diligence and priced through indemnities.
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a Seller awareness qualifier on specific warranties only, limited to named individuals after reasonable enquiry. Add an express statement that the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice any claim.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts (DL §2):** about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Change-control consent under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. No final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions as at 22 Sept.
- **Issue:** the Seller offers reasonable endeavours only, and the condition is deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. That is exactly the consent-on-delivery position the playbook rejects. A consent subject to unsatisfied cl 11.3 conditions may be ineffective, which would leave a 30% customer exposed.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Completion condition: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The Seller must deliver evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
  - Upgrade the effort obligation beyond reasonable endeavours and give the Buyer a right to participate in consent communications.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts (DL §3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding as at 22 Sept. Change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2 apply. Not repaid and no discharge supplied.
- **Issue:** a release "following Completion" means we would complete with live security and a change-of-control trigger. The Seller offers no undertaking and no payout mechanism.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter (a fresh figure, since the ~AUD 3.2m is stale) with a daily rate.
  - Repay directly from Completion funds to Riverlark.
  - Deliver executed security releases (including PPSR releases) at Completion.
  - The amount must flow through Debt in the price mechanics.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking/deed of release AND Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

### 10. Employee bonuses: funds flow (DL §5)
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). They are not in the funds flow, and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Issue:** the cover note's statement that bonuses are "a matter for the Seller and … not separately itemised" is precisely the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the Company pays them after Completion, we bear the cost.
- **Push back:**
  - Include the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding) as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt/Transaction Costs, or otherwise funded by the Seller.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost not deducted.
  - Seek confirmation of which on-costs apply. We should not assume that they do or do not.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4)
- **Facts:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is not independently bank-verified. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Issue:** an indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. That risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials, which could lead to infringement claims, loss of use and remediation costs.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to all Losses from any failure of the Company to own or be entitled to use the Ironquay/SOW3 materials.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: require cleared payment evidence plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general regime.
  - Treat the AUD 180k figure as unverified in both directions. Request bank evidence and an Ironquay statement.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Facts:** a download link went to an unintended external address, potentially exposing ~1,240 records. Access, scope and notification are all undetermined, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Issue:** the cover note's "not expected to be material" is an unsupported characterisation. Equally, we should not treat the incident as a confirmed breach, assume harm, assume a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller covenants to preserve all logs and evidence and to complete a proper investigation.
  - Regular updates before Completion, with Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - A specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, outside the general cap, basket and disclosure.
  - Delete any wording that would treat the matter as immaterial or as fully disclosed.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DL §8): AUD 330k
- **Issue:** the Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs", but its own DL §8 says the material does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. The three related renewals should be read together.
- **Push back:** do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation, and do not ourselves assume Debt treatment or a price deduction. Request the contracts, approvals, timing and termination rights. Then decide whether a warranty, conduct-of-business covenant, Debt/working-capital treatment or specific indemnity is appropriate.

### 14. Tax and IP: "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. We should assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Push back:** reject the statement that they are settled. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories, not folded into the general regime through cl 12.3/13. Their limits are to be negotiated, not imported by default.

### 15. Title evidence (DL §10)
- **Issue:** DD-012 is the Company's own register, a supplied internal source and not independent proof. DL §10 itself concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:**
  - Require independent evidence: ASIC searches, share certificates, PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares, issue/transfer history and board minutes.
  - Require evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (constitution, board resolution).
  - Require confirmation of no encumbrances (tying in with the Riverlark release).
  - Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime and be unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.

### 16. Lower-priority items: lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9)
The Seller's descriptions (a notification-only obligation, and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale) are plausible. They are still the Seller's reading, so confirm against the underlying documents and add a warranty that no consent is required for the sale.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "FINAL / agreed / market" | Asserted | Reject; confirm in writing that nothing is agreed |
| 1 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m**; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **5k / 50k tipping** |
| 3 | General period | 18 months, applied to all Claims | **24 months**; remove the "all Claims" override |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **100% cap, ≥6 years**, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | Limits apply to "all Claims" | **Full carve-out, non-negotiable** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete**; at most named-person Seller awareness |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent + cl 11.3 evidence as CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **AUD 420k + on-costs line item / Seller-funded** |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity | **Broad IP-ownership indemnity + SOW3 cure** |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve, investigate, update; specific indemnity**; no assumed outcome |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first**; no automatic characterisation |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Open; separate categories** |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title, authority and encumbrance evidence** |

**Immediate actions:**
1. Send a holding response rejecting the "final/agreed" characterisation.
2. Request a bring-down of the 22 September disclosures, covering Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation status and Sandbar documents.
3. Prepare our mark-up on the playbook starting positions.
4. Escalate to Amelia Frost only if the deal team wants authority to deploy the cap or time-limit fallbacks. Any such authority should be draft-specific and conditional on the rest of the package conforming.

The fraud carve-out is outside anyone's authority to concede, so it should be presented to the Seller as a fixed requirement.

That is exactly the consent-on-delivery position the playbook rejects. A consent subject to unsatisfied cl 11.3 conditions may be ineffective, which would leave a 30% customer exposed.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Completion condition: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The Seller must deliver evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
  - Upgrade the effort obligation beyond reasonable endeavours and give the Buyer a right to participate in consent communications.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts (DL §3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding as at 22 Sept. Change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2 apply. Not repaid and no discharge supplied.
- **Issue:** a release "following Completion" means we would complete with live security and a change-of-control trigger. The Seller offers no undertaking and no payout mechanism.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter (a fresh figure, since the ~AUD 3.2m is stale) with a daily rate.
  - Repay directly from Completion funds to Riverlark.
  - Deliver executed security releases (including PPSR releases) at Completion.
  - The amount must flow through Debt in the price mechanics.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking/deed of release AND Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

### 10. Employee bonuses: funds flow (DL §5)
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses (DD-005). They are not in the funds flow, and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Issue:** the cover note's statement that bonuses are "a matter for the Seller and … not separately itemised" is precisely the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the Company pays them after Completion, we bear the cost.
- **Push back:**
  - Include the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding) as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt/Transaction Costs, or otherwise funded by the Seller.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost not deducted.
  - Seek confirmation of which on-costs apply. We should not assume that they do or do not.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4)
- **Facts:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is not independently bank-verified. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Issue:** an indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. That risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials, which could lead to infringement claims, loss of use and remediation costs.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to all Losses from any failure of the Company to own or be entitled to use the Ironquay/SOW3 materials.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: require cleared payment evidence plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general regime.
  - Treat the AUD 180k figure as unverified in both directions. Request bank evidence and an Ironquay statement.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Facts:** a download link went to an unintended external address, potentially exposing ~1,240 records. Access, scope and notification are all undetermined, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Issue:** the cover note's "not expected to be material" is an unsupported characterisation. Equally, we should not treat the incident as a confirmed breach, assume harm, assume a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller covenants to preserve all logs and evidence and to complete a proper investigation.
  - Regular updates before Completion, with Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - A specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident, outside the general cap, basket and disclosure.
  - Delete any wording that would treat the matter as immaterial or as fully disclosed.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DL §8): AUD 330k
- **Issue:** the Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs", but its own DL §8 says the material does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. The three related renewals should be read together.
- **Push back:** do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation, and do not ourselves assume Debt treatment or a price deduction. Request the contracts, approvals, timing and termination rights. Then decide whether a warranty, conduct-of-business covenant, Debt/working-capital treatment or specific indemnity is appropriate.

### 14. Tax and IP: "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. We should assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Push back:** reject the statement that they are settled. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories, not folded into the general regime through cl 12.3/13. Their limits are to be negotiated, not imported by default.

### 15. Title evidence (DL §10)
- **Issue:** DD-012 is the Company's own register, a supplied internal source and not independent proof. DL §10 itself concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:**
  - Require independent evidence: ASIC searches, share certificates, PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares, issue/transfer history and board minutes.
  - Require evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (constitution, board resolution).
  - Require confirmation of no encumbrances (tying in with the Riverlark release).
  - Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime and be unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.

### 16. Lower-priority items: lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9)
The Seller's descriptions (a notification-only obligation, and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale) are plausible. They are still the Seller's reading, so confirm against the underlying documents and add a warranty that no consent is required for the sale.
